solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Casual juries condemned old dictator

indicators.note: condemned suggests the jurors' words are wrecked, so their letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A slapdash jury convicts an ancient strongman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned' is the anagram signal working on the letters of CASUAL JURIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman general was made dictator of Rome before his assassination in 44 BC.

clue.text: Second judge uncertain

parts.note: iffy is informal for doubtful or uncertain

explanation.surface: A referee or judge hesitates for a moment, unsure of the call.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a very short moment of time.

clue.text: Cat more domesticated? Not his

parts.note: the lion is one of the big cats
tamer means more domesticated

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pet cat is getting tamer, and is told it is not his.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the circus act: the big cat becomes tamer, yet the trainer himself does not.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer whose job is training big cats to behave docilely in the ring.

clue.text: Illicit to be drunk here

definitions.meaning: payments made secretly and illegally are said to pass this way
someone who has drunk far too much ends up collapsed on the floor beneath the dining surface

explanation.surface: A warning that some illegal drinking goes on in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both covert bribes and being so intoxicated one slides to the floor.

clue.text: Arrive, extremely lively and attractive

parts.note: to come is to arrive

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outside letters of lively

explanation.surface: Someone turns up, very lively and good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Comely is an old-fashioned synonym for good-looking, usually of a woman.

clue.text: Intemperance by immoral girl that's costly at airport

parts.note: excess is overindulgence, lack of restraint
baggage is a dated, disparaging term for a shameless young woman

explanation.surface: An overindulgent, loose-living woman proves an expensive companion at the airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage over the airline's weight allowance must be paid for at check-in.

clue.text: Church vestment used in several baptisms

indicators.note: used in says the answer sits within the letters of several baptisms

explanation.surface: A church garment worn at several christenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A long white linen robe worn by clergy during services such as Mass.

clue.text: Look through crumbling arches

indicators.note: crumbling arches fall apart, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone examines a ruin's decaying arches.
explanation.definitionFit: To search a place is to go through it carefully looking for something.

clue.text: Lots of water, litres, to be taken during meal

indicators.note: taken during a meal means put inside the word for the meal

parts.note: food stands for a meal

explanation.surface: Plenty of water, litres of it, drunk with dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An overflow of water onto normally dry land is a deluge.

clue.text: Gruesome as taxi is squashed by horse

indicators.note: the taxi word squashed by the horse word is held tightly inside it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a taxi crushed by a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre describes something ghastly, dwelling on death and horror.

clue.text: Mythical creature doesn't have one on the other hand

indicators.note: doesn't have means the creature's name loses a letter

parts.note: the yeti is the legendary abominable snowman of the Himalayas
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A legendary beast lacks something it might otherwise have.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet works as a contrastive conjunction, meaning however or nevertheless.

clue.text: Luxury car finished ends up on its roof

parts.note: a Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, is a luxury car
over means finished

explanation.surface: A wrecked luxury car finishes upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle that flips in a crash turns over and lands upside down.

clue.text: Day cutting grape plant is profitable for wine

indicators.note: the day abbreviation cutting into the plant word goes inside it

parts.note: grapes grow on a vine
something profitable pays

explanation.surface: A day spent pruning vines turns a profit for the winemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'country wine', a regional category ranked above table wine.

clue.text: Swelling: hospital creates paperwork

parts.note: a bump is a swelling

explanation.surface: A patient's lump leads the hospital to generate a pile of forms.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for tedious official documents and forms.

clue.text: Next to boy, insect buzzing round

indicators.note: round means the insect's name goes around the boy's

parts.note: the bee is the buzzing insect
Sid is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A bee buzzes around a lad standing nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside is a preposition meaning alongside or at the side of.

clue.text: The place for substitute judges?

definitions.meaning: in football and other sports, reserve players sit on a seat beside the pitch
judges or magistrates collectively are called by the name of the seat they occupy in court

explanation.surface: Asking where stand-in judges go.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sports team's seat for reserves and the judiciary collectively.

clue.text: Strip club that's disreputable on street

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or nightclub

explanation.surface: A sleazy strip club located on a street.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest someone is to strip or deprive them of something.

clue.text: Hungriest to change? Absolutely

indicators.note: to change asks for the letters of hungriest to be reordered

explanation.surface: Asked if the hungriest should change, someone replies emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges the letters of HUNGRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: As an exclamation the phrase means certainly, of course, an emphatic yes.

clue.text: Fairy putting an end to himself

indicators.note: an end to himself means the closing letters of that word

explanation.surface: A fairy commits suicide.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'end' of 'himself' is its last three letters, not just the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are small mischievous supernatural beings of folklore.

clue.text: In merriment see to mattress

indicators.note: In merriment says the little word to is placed within the word for merriment

parts.note: fun is merriment

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully attends to a mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese-style padded mattress laid on the floor or on a low frame.

clue.text: Girl, black, put out of action

parts.note: Di is a girl's name
sable is the heraldic word for black

explanation.surface: A woman in black is incapacitated.
explanation.definitionFit: To disable something is to stop it working or render it useless.

clue.text: Loan for boat

definitions.meaning: an advance of money, as in subbing someone a fiver
short for submarine, an underwater vessel

explanation.surface: Borrowing money to buy a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an advance on pay, and a clipped form of submarine.

clue.text: A carriage returns separately

indicators.note: returns says the carriage word is read backwards

parts.note: a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A carriage comes back in pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means individually, away from each other.

clue.text: Refuse to agree reading in church is instructive experience

parts.note: to object is to protest or refuse to agree
the lesson is a Bible passage read aloud during a service

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a church reading and learns from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical example that teaches a principle by demonstration.
